security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline code, relative documentation links, and schema terminology. Two findings are confirmed because the skill recommends local Python connector helpers that run with user-derived values. No prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Optional Python connector helpers execute local commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running helpers, avoid shell interpolation, and pass entity values as argv.

remediation.issue: Connector helpers may perform live public lookups.
remediation.suggestion: Document network access for Wikidata, pageviews, and GDELT helpers, and keep an offline user-to-run path.

remediation.issue: Saved entity profile paths are derived from entity names.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize slugs and reject path separators before writing any profile under memory/entities.

content.user_title: Optimize Entity Presence for AI Search
content.value_statement: Search and AI systems often confuse weak or inconsistent entities. This skill audits identity signals and creates a clear action plan.
actual_capabilities: Audits entity recognition across Knowledge Graph, Wikidata, Wikipedia, schema, and AI systems.
Scores 47 signals across six entity signal categories.
Produces a canonical entity profile with sameAs links, identifiers, disambiguation notes, and sourced claims.
Creates a prioritized action plan for structured data, Wikidata, mentions, and content gaps.
Provides handoff guidance to markup, GEO content, and authority workflows.
Flags privacy and lawful basis checks before storing profiles for people.
limitations: Cannot query live search or AI tools without tool access or user-provided results.
Does not create weak or promotional Wikipedia content.
Legal and GDPR guidance is advisory, not legal advice.
Requires reliable sources to validate factual claims and knowledge graph entries.

use_cases.title: Audit Brand Recognition
use_cases.description: Find gaps in how search engines and AI systems identify a company, product, or public brand.

use_cases.title: Prepare Knowledge Graph Work
use_cases.description: Build a source-backed entity profile before updating Schema.org, Wikidata, or sameAs references.

use_cases.title: Resolve Entity Confusion
use_cases.description: Create a disambiguation plan when AI systems mix one entity with competitors, acronyms, or similar names.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Entity Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit entity presence for [entity name] at [domain]. Use the sources I provide and mark unknown signals as user-to-run.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Canonical Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a canonical entity profile for [entity name]. Include type, official URL, sameAs links, identifiers, claims, sources, and disambiguation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Entity Confusion
prompt_templates.prompt: AI systems confuse [entity name] with [similar entity]. Audit the signals and recommend fixes for names, schema, profiles, and content.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Knowledge Graph Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 90-day entity optimization roadmap for [entity]. Prioritize Wikidata, structured data, authority mentions, AI recognition tests, and downstream handoffs.

output_examples.input: Audit entity presence for Acme Analytics, a B2B SaaS product.
output_examples.output: The audit finds partial recognition, missing Wikidata coverage, incomplete leadership schema, and weak AI descriptions. The top actions focus on sameAs links, source-backed facts, and an About page definition.

output_examples.input: AI systems confuse our brand with a larger company using the same acronym.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a consistent qualified name, unique Schema.org identifiers, stronger official profiles, and disambiguation copy across high-authority pages.

output_examples.input: Prepare an entity profile before handing work to a markup specialist.
output_examples.output: The output includes a neutral definition, canonical URL, official profiles, identifiers, verified claims, unresolved source gaps, and handoff notes for schema implementation.

best_practices: Provide the official domain, profiles, known identifiers, and trusted source links before starting.
Separate verified facts from assumptions, and date claims that may change.
Use the action plan to update owned pages before requesting Wikidata or Wikipedia work.
anti_patterns: Do not invent citations, founders, awards, or identifiers to make an entity look stronger.
Do not treat promotional copy as a neutral entity definition.
Do not write profiles for people without checking privacy and lawful basis requirements.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It optimizes machine-readable entity identity for search engines, knowledge graphs, and AI answer systems.

faq.question: Does it create Wikidata or Wikipedia pages?
faq.answer: It prepares source-backed recommendations. It advises against weak, promotional, or conflict-of-interest edits.

faq.question: Can it test ChatGPT, Claude, or Perplexity directly?
faq.answer: Only when the host has suitable tools. Otherwise it asks the user to run tests and report results.

faq.question: What inputs improve the audit?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include the entity name, domain, profiles, target topics, competitors, existing schema, and known confusion cases.

faq.question: Is this the same as page-level AI citation optimization?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on canonical entity identity. Page-level citation readiness belongs in a GEO content workflow.

faq.question: Can it help with personal brands?
faq.answer: Yes, but it asks for privacy and lawful basis checks before saving profiles for individuals.
